newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine army, rebels urged not to use artillery.
newsitem.headline: Philippine army, rebels urged not to use artillery.

text.p: Christian and Moslem leaders in the southern Philippines urged the military and Islamic rebels on Tuesday not to use artillery to avoid civilian casualties.
The Southern Philippine Council for Peace and Development (SPCPD) issued the call as soldiers pursued retreating rebels after more than a week of fighting in which more than 80 people were killed.

"We appeal to the armed forces leadership and to the the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) to refrain from using heavy weapons, artillery and weapons of mass destruction," the SPCD said in a resolution sent to the military and the MILF.
The resolution was approved by Christian and Moslem leaders comprising the SPCPD, an administrative body set up by President Fidel Ramos to supervise development of the southern islands.
Reacting to the SPCPD call, southern military commander Lieutenant General Romeo Padiernos said: "It will be foolhardy for the armed forces to pursue these groups with empty hands."

The military used bomber planes and artillery in driving the MILF out of one of its major camps last week. The military said 76 rebels and seven soldiers died in the clashes, which displaced more than 30,000 villagers.

The SPCPD is headed by former Moslem rebel chief Nur Misuari, who signed a peace deal with Manila last year ending a 24-year separatist revolt led by the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MNLF), which Misuari led.
The MNLF was the mainstream rebel force in Mindanao until it accepted peace with Manila. The MILF was not a party to the deal but has begun separate peace talks with the government.
